pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Colorado State Electrical Board uses PSI Services LLC for the electrical examination program. The Colorado Journeyman Wireman exam is a computer-based licensing examination for candidates pursuing the journeyman level in Colorado. The exam measures entry-level competence across electrical job task areas and is designed to evaluate whether a candidate can apply electrical knowledge safely and correctly. Effective August 1, 2026, Colorado electrical exam questions are consistent with the 2026 National Electrical Code. The 2026 National Electrical Code book and Formula Page are provided at the test center. Candidates may not write, highlight, underline, or index on the provided references and may not use any other materials in the examination room. The Colorado Journeyman Wireman examination includes 90 scored items with 240 minutes of testing time. The passing standard listed in the candidate information is 70%, which equals 63 correct scored items. The exam may also include up to 10 non-scored items, with additional time added for those items.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Non-scored items are used for exam development and do not count toward the final pass or fail result. The Colorado Journeyman Wireman content outline includes the following exam areas: general electrical knowledge, services, feeders and branch circuits, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, conductors and cables, raceways and boxes, special occupancies, special equipment, electrical devices, motors, transformers, photovoltaics, and electrical calculations. A well-rounded study plan should include both code lookup practice and trade-concept review because the exam can require candidates to connect installation facts to the correct NEC rules and formulas.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Colorado Journeyman Wireman exam uses provided references at the test center. The 2026 National Electrical Code book and Formula Page are provided for exams based on the 2026 NEC. Candidates may not bring personal reference materials into the examination room, and the provided references may not be written in, highlighted, underlined, or indexed. For preparation, this makes code-navigation practice especially important. A tabbed personal copy of the 2026 NEC can help you learn where key articles, tables, definitions, wiring method rules, grounding and bonding provisions, motor requirements, service calculations, and special occupancy requirements are located. The goal is not only to read the NEC, but to become more comfortable moving through the code language and recognizing which section applies to the question being asked. Because the exam references the NEC and includes calculation-based content, candidates should study both rule application and electrical formulas.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Formula Page provided at the test center supports exam work, but candidates are still responsible for knowing how to use electrical theory formulas and how to apply them to practical electrical problems.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t:
Colorado journeyman electrician licensing is handled through the Colorado State Electrical Board within the Division of Professions and Occupations. Candidates pursuing the journeyman level should follow the state application process, document qualifying experience, complete the exam process, and submit licensing materials as required by the Board.
A typical licensing path includes gaining qualifying electrical experience, preparing the required documentation, applying through the Colorado licensing system, scheduling the examination through PSI after eligibility or registration requirements are met, taking the Colorado Journeyman Wireman exam, and completing the remaining state licensing requirements after examination.
Candidates should keep careful records of supervised electrical work experience, dates, categories of work, employer information, and supporting documentation. Experience documentation is an important part of electrical licensing, and incomplete or inaccurate records can slow down the licensing process.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Colorado’s journeyman electrician license is associated with documented electrical construction wiring experience for light, heat, and power. Journeyman applicants are generally expected to document 8,000 hours of electrical construction wiring experience earned over no less than four years. A portion of that experience must include commercial or industrial work. Colorado also has education requirements that may apply to apprentices based on registration date and state rules. Candidates should make sure their experience, education, and documentation align with Colorado State Electrical Board requirements before scheduling or completing licensing steps. The Colorado electrical licensing process is state regulated, and the examination is one part of the overall path. Passing the exam alone does not automatically grant a license. Candidates must still meet the Board’s qualification standards, submit required documentation, and complete the licensing process through the proper state channels.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: For exam preparation, candidates should focus on the 2026 NEC cycle when preparing for testing effective August 1, 2026. Studying from outdated code material can create confusion because article wording, tables, definitions, and installation requirements may change between code cycles. This Ultimate Combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code to support preparation for the 2026 NEC exam cycle.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: The Colorado Journeyman Wireman exam covers a broad range of electrical knowledge areas. Candidates should prepare for questions involving general electrical principles, services, feeders, branch circuits, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, conductor sizing, raceway and box rules, special occupancies, special equipment, electrical devices, motors, transformers, photovoltaics, and calculations. Because the exam includes 90 scored questions over 240 minutes, pacing matters. Candidates should practice reading each question carefully, identifying the installation condition, determining whether the question is asking for a definition, rule, calculation, exception, table value, or equipment requirement, and then selecting the best answer. Rushing can lead to missed details, especially in calculation and code-reference questions. Candidates should use their study time to learn article organization, chapter structure, table locations, and common code pathways. The 2026 Journeyman Electrician Flash Cards are useful for short study sessions, warmups, review breaks, and repeated exposure to important terms and concepts. Flash cards can help reinforce vocabulary, formulas, and code-related ideas that are easier to retain through repetition. pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Colorado State Electrical Board licenses, registers, and regulates electricians, apprentices, and electrical contractors in Colorado. The Board’s licensing exams are administered through PSI Services LLC. The Colorado electrical exam program includes exams for Residential Wireman, Journeyman Wireman, Master Electrician, and the Colorado Journeyman Wireman exam for apprentices with six or more years of apprentice registration. The Colorado Master Electrician exam is a computer-based exam administered by PSI. The current PSI candidate bulletin lists the Master Electrician exam with 90 scored items and 240 minutes of testing time. The bulletin also lists up to 10 non-scored items with 30 additional minutes. The listed passing standard is 70%, which equals 63 correct scored items.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Master Electrician examination content outline includes General Electrical Knowledge, Services, Feeders, and Branch Circuits, Grounding and Bonding, Overcurrent Protection, Conductors and Cables, Raceways and Boxes, Special Conditions, Special Occupancies, Special Equipment, Electrical Devices, Motors, Transformers, and Electrical Calculations. Grounding and bonding is one of the largest listed categories, and calculations are also a significant part of the exam outline. The PSI bulletin states that examination questions are currently consistent with the 2023 National Electrical Code. Effective August 1, 2026, the bulletin states that all examination questions are consistent with the 2026 National Electrical Code, and the 2026 National Electrical Code book and Formula Page are provided at the test center. This product is based on the 2026 NEC for candidates preparing for the 2026 code cycle. PSI provides score results immediately after completion of the examination. Candidates who do not pass may reregister under PSI’s scheduling rules.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Passing the exam is part of the licensing process, and applicants must still meet the Colorado State Electrical Board’s license qualification requirements.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Colorado Master Electrician exam uses reference materials during the examination. The PSI candidate bulletin states that the National Electrical Code book and Formula Page are provided at the test center. For exams effective August 1, 2026, the bulletin identifies the 2026 National Electrical Code book and Formula Page as the test center-provided references. Candidates may not use other materials during the exam and may not write, highlight, underline, or index on the test center-provided references. This makes preparation especially important. Even though reference materials are available during testing, candidates should not expect to rely on custom notes, personal tabs, loose papers, study guides, or personal reference books in the exam room. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs included in this Ultimate Combo is a study tool for building familiarity before exam day. Tabs help candidates practice moving through the NEC during preparation, even though the test center provides the exam reference.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Studying with a tabbed NEC can help candidates learn article locations, table organization, definitions, exceptions, wiring method rules, grounding and bonding structure, and calculation references. An open-book exam still demands strong preparation. Candidates must know how to read the question, identify the code issue, find the correct section, apply the rule, and manage time. The strongest candidates do not simply search the book from scratch on every question. They enter the exam with a working understanding of how the NEC is organized and how common master electrician topics are tested.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Colorado Master Electrician candidates must meet the licensing requirements established by the Colorado State Electrical Board. Practical experience must be documented on the Board’s Affidavit of Experience form and completed by the electrical contractor supervising the work performed. Candidates should gather accurate work documentation before beginning the license application process. Colorado lists several pathways for Master Electrician experience qualification. Candidates may qualify with 10,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 5 years; a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from an accredited college or university plus 2,000 hours of construction experience earned in no less than 1 year; graduation from an electrical trade school or community college plus 8,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 4 years; or 2,000 hours of experience earned in no less than 1 year in addition to the Journeyman Wireman requirements.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: For the path based on additional experience after the Journeyman Wireman requirements, some hours must include planning and layout, and some must include supervision while in possession of a Journeyman Electrician license. The Colorado licensing page notes that it is not possible to go directly from Apprentice or Residential Wireman to Master when using experience to qualify for the Master license. Candidates should review which pathway applies to their background before submitting an application. After meeting the qualification requirements and completing the exam process, applicants file the appropriate license application with the Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations. PSI scheduling is handled through the Colorado electrical examination program. Candidates should use the same legal name that appears on their identification, follow PSI’s scheduling instructions, and bring the required identification to the examination site.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Colorado’s State Electrical Board regulates electricians, apprentices, and electrical contractors. The Board’s mission includes protecting public health and safety by enforcing Colorado electrical statutes. Colorado recognizes license and registration categories that include apprentice registration, Residential Wireman, Journeyman Electrician, Master Electrician, and Electrical Contractor registration. To perform electrical contracting in Colorado, a business must be registered as an Electrical Contractor with the State of Colorado. The contractor must hold or employ a licensed master electrician to serve as the responsible individual for the company. The master electrician and company owner, when they are separate individuals, must sign the required acknowledgment of responsibility. The selected master electrician may serve as the responsible party for one company only. Colorado also requires electricians and electrical contractors to renew on the state’s renewal cycle.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Active Residential Wireman, Journeyman Electrician, and Master Electrician license holders must complete at least 24 hours of continuing education during each 3-year license period. License holders should track renewal dates, complete required continuing education, and keep their contact information current with the Division of Professions and Occupations.
